functional.text: A user can publish a post: text plus optional photos/videos.
A user sees a home feed of recent posts from accounts they follow, newest first, paginated 20 at a time (infinite scroll).

non_functional.text: Feed page latency < 300 ms at p99; read-heavy (~20 feed loads per post).
Eventually consistent: a new post reaches followers' feeds within ~10 s.
Highly available reads; a slow fan-out must never block publishing, and a stored post is never lost.
Media is served quickly worldwide without passing through the app servers.

assumptions.text: 200M DAU, 10 feed opens and 0.5 posts per user per day; peak = 2× average.
Average 300 followers; a few thousand accounts have tens of millions.
~30% of posts carry media, ~1 MB each after compression.

api.notes: The app then PUTs bytes straight to storage.
Returns once the post is stored; distribution is asynchronous. Idempotency-Key header.
Cursor = last seen post_id (time-sortable), stable while new posts arrive.

data.name: posts
data.fields: post_id (PK, time-sortable), author_id, text, media_urls, created_at
data.why: Fetched by id in batches; scales horizontally by post_id.

data.name: follows
data.fields: follower_id, followee_id, created_at; indexed both directions
data.why: Graph edges queried as 'followers of X' (fan-out) and 'who X follows' (celebrity merge).

data.name: feeds
data.why: Precomputed per-user feed: one lookup per feed load.

data.name: media
data.fields: media_id, owner_id, object key, renditions, status
data.why: Bytes in object storage behind a CDN; the post only stores URLs.

deep_dives.title: Celebrity threshold: where to draw it and what happens at the line

options.name: Fan out to everyone anyway
options.cons: minutes of backlog per post; delays everyone else's posts

options.name: Fixed follower threshold (~100k); merge at read
options.cons: accounts crossing the line need a policy

options.name: Dynamic: decide per post from follower count × active followers
options.cons: harder to reason about and test

deep_dives.choice: Fixed threshold of ~100k followers; skip fan-out above it and merge at read time
deep_dives.why: Followers follow only a handful of such accounts and their recent posts sit in the post cache, so the merge is cheap. When an account crosses the threshold a flag flips; entries already pushed simply age out of feeds.

deep_dives.title: Pagination

options.name: offset/limit
options.cons: new posts shift pages: duplicates and gaps

deep_dives.why: Infinite scroll on a feed that changes every second.

deep_dives.title: Feed cache memory and inactive users

options.name: Precompute feeds for every user
options.cons: ~800 GB of RAM, much of it for people who never open the app

options.name: Precompute only for users active in the last 30 days; rebuild on return
options.cons: the first load after a long absence is a slow pull

deep_dives.choice: Precompute only for recently active users; rebuild a returning user's feed by pulling once
deep_dives.why: Fan-out workers check an 'active' bit and skip the rest, cutting both cache memory and insert rate; one slow load per returning user is acceptable.

wrapup.bottlenecks: Fan-out queue backlog on busy days (scale workers, prioritise recently active users), hot post bodies (replicated post cache), feed cache memory (ids only, trim to 500, skip users inactive for 30 days).
wrapup.failures: Feed cache node lost: rebuild that user's feed on demand by pulling from followees. Fan-out workers down: posts are safe in the store, the outbox and queue retain work and feeds catch up late. CDN miss storm: origin shield in front of object storage.
wrapup.monitoring: Feed p99 latency, cache hit ratio, fan-out queue lag (publish → visible time), worker error rate, CDN hit ratio, orphaned-upload count.
wrapup.scale: Shard the feed cache by user_id, add queue partitions and workers, lower the celebrity threshold, precompute only for active users, multi-region read replicas.
wrapup.future: Ranked feed (candidate generation from this cache + a ranking service), ads injection, notifications for close friends.

parts.title: Post write and storage
parts.problem: Accept ~1.2k posts/s (peak ~2.4k) durably, give each a time-sortable id, and acknowledge the author at once, while never losing the hand-off to the delivery step.

options.name: Single SQL table with auto-increment ids
options.cons: one primary takes every write; ids are not globally unique once sharded

options.name: Wide-column store keyed by post_id, Snowflake-style ids, outbox row in the same write
options.pros: scales writes horizontally; ids sort by time; hand-off survives crashes
options.cons: no cross-row transactions; needs an id generator per node

options.name: Write post, then publish to the queue from the request
options.cons: a crash between the two writes loses the fan-out (dual write)

parts.choice: Wide-column posts store keyed by a time-sortable id, with an outbox entry that a relay forwards to the queue
parts.why: 2.4k writes/s and 100M posts/day need horizontal writes; time-sortable ids give cursors for free; the outbox makes 'stored but never distributed' impossible, which N3 asks for.

parts.title: Fan-out: delivering posts to followers
parts.problem: Get each new post into followers' feeds within ~10 s when the average author has 300 followers but a few have tens of millions; decide whether feeds are built at write time, read time or both.

options.name: Fan-out on read (pull)
options.cons: each feed load queries ~300 authors and merges: too slow at ~46k loads/s

options.name: Fan-out on write (push)
options.pros: a feed load becomes one cache read
options.cons: ~350k inserts/s; one 40M-follower post is 40M inserts and backs up the queue

options.name: Hybrid: push for normal accounts, pull for huge ones
options.pros: cheap reads and bounded write cost
options.cons: two code paths and a merge at read time

parts.choice: Hybrid fan-out: workers push post ids into followers' feed lists, except for accounts above ~100k followers, which are pulled at read time
parts.why: Reads outnumber posts ~20:1, so precomputing is worth ~350k cache inserts/s; skipping the few huge accounts keeps the queue draining inside the 10 s budget (N2).

parts.title: Feed read and ranking
parts.problem: Serve a 20-post feed page in < 300 ms at ~46k loads/s: read the precomputed ids, merge posts from followed celebrities, hydrate the bodies and decide the order.

options.name: Hydrate every id from the posts store
options.cons: 20 store reads per page, ~1M reads/s at peak; hot posts hammer one partition

options.name: Post cache in front of the store, batch get, merge celebrity posts, then order
options.pros: one cache round trip for bodies; hot posts stay in memory

options.name: Inline ML ranking service on every load
options.cons: adds latency and a dependency; out of scope for v1

parts.choice: Read ids from the feed cache, merge followed celebrities' recent posts, batch-hydrate from a post cache, order by time behind a scorer hook
parts.why: Two cache round trips fit easily in 300 ms; the scorer hook lets ranking replace chronological order later without changing storage.

parts.title: Media upload and delivery
parts.problem: Photos and videos are most of the bytes (≈ 30 TB/day) and are viewed worldwide; keep them off the post and feed services.

options.name: Upload through the post service and store in the database
options.cons: app servers stream gigabytes; the database bloats

options.name: Presigned upload straight to object storage, renditions by workers, served by a CDN
options.pros: app servers only sign URLs; bytes travel edge ↔ storage
options.cons: upload and post creation are two steps; orphaned uploads need cleanup

parts.choice: Presigned direct upload to object storage, workers create renditions, a CDN serves them
parts.why: Keeps ~30 TB/day of bytes off the services; posts carry only URLs, so feed responses stay small and the CDN absorbs global reads.
